items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions John Collins as someone Frank Sinatra used, but the interviewee (Juan Tizol) does not confirm working with or knowing John Collins personally, only discussing the band's dynamic with Sinatra and mentioning Sweets Edison.

ctx.x: Yeah. I was in the air.

Were there other musicians from the jazz world also working for Frank? I know he usually likes to have jazz musicians in the orchestra. I know he's used John Collins, Al Viola, and he used to have Ziggy Elman and Dave Barber and Herbie Hamer -- he had a lot of jazz musicians backing him. Were there other jazz people from jazz when you were working with him?

Well, when we worked with Sinatra, the band didn't do much, unless once in awhile, somebody had to take a little extra chorus, because Sinatra did the singing, and naturally, he didn't need anyone to back him up on something where he was playing a solo. The only one he used to once in awhile play something in the same recording was Sweets -- the trumpet player.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: one recording I did with Nat also was an album called 'After Midnight.' ... This album featured Edison Hugh Tizol

ctx.x: Yeah, I had to do it -- yeah, so I would go home and just really get into it every night, and really practice and study, because I knew that when I left there I had to cut it. And I had so much to say, I had to get it out. And so I would go to my room and get it out, you know. But it was just, as I said, one of those things. Speaking of recording, one recording I did with Nat also was an album called 'After Midnight.' And I had quite a few solos in this album, which I liked. This album featured Edison Hugh Tizol…
